title: Brahman: Meaning and Context
excerpt: Brahman is the Sanskrit term for ultimate reality in Vedanta, not a member of the priestly class, which is a different word.

quick_answer.question: What does Brahman mean?
quick_answer.answer: Brahman means ultimate reality in Vedanta. Advaita says the self is not other than it. Other schools describe a real relationship rather than simple identity.

intro: Brahman, in this philosophical sense, is the ultimate that Vedanta argues about. It is not a mood and not the caste title brahmin.

sections.heading: What does Brahman mean?
sections.content:
Advaita treats brahman as without a second, so the apparent world of separate selves is ignorance. Theistic Vedanta can speak of brahman in personal terms and refuse the claim that devotion is only a ladder to be discarded. The spelling is the same in English for more than one Sanskrit form, which is why context matters.

The neighboring page is [the Vedanta explainer](/articles/what-is-vedanta/). Treat that link as part of the argument, not as decoration.

sections.heading: Where does the word come from?
sections.content:
Upanishadic language gestures more than it defines. Commentaries do the defining, and they fight. Britannica's brahman article keeps the philosophical sense distinct from other uses of similar words.

A wider map lives at the [ancient wisdom topic](/topics/ancient-wisdom/). Dates and school names matter, because a recent American presentation is often described as if it had no date.

sections.heading: How is the word misused?
sections.content:
If a sentence says everything is brahman, ask which school and what follows for ethics. A metaphysical slogan is not a reason to ignore a person in front of you.

If you want a narrower practical or comparative page, use [Atman and Brahman](/articles/atman-vs-brahman/). You can understand the description without joining a group or buying a course.

sections.heading: What should a careful reader refuse?
sections.content:
Do not equate the word with the universe in a casual physics sense. Do not treat a class affirmation as an Upanishad. The claim is doctrinal.

Readers in the United States often meet a simpler version of the same idea in a class, an app, or a short video. Name that simpler version instead of pretending it is the whole tradition. Traditional teaching, personal report, and research stay in separate sentences on this site. The [editorial policy](/editorial-policy/) is the rule. The [disclaimer](/disclaimer/) applies whenever a sentence leans toward health, safety, or a promised transformation. The [corrections](/corrections/) page is how to challenge a factual mistake. Name the school, the text, or the century whenever a sentence would otherwise float free of history. A reader may stop at the definition when that is all the question required.

key_takeaways: Brahman is a traditional term with a narrower meaning than popular English often allows.
Schools and modern classes do not all use it the same way.
The glossary states the limit. Longer pages carry the argument.

faq.question: Is Brahman a scientific term?
faq.answer: No. It is a term of Vedanta, not a scientific variable.

faq.question: Where is the longer page?
faq.answer: Read the atman entry and the Vedanta topic.
